# London police arrest 48 as hundreds protest Palestine Action ban

*Demonstrations in London and Edinburgh come days before a UK Supreme Court appeal challenging the group’s proscription.*

Save

Share

![A pro-Palestinian activist is carried away by police officers after being arrested during a protest outside the US Embassy in London](/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/afp_6ae629da1790-1793468890.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)

A pro-Palestinian activist is carried away by police officers after being arrested during a protest outside the US embassy in London on Saturday [AFP]

[![](/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/2017-06-08T131939Z_1189275883_RC11B0FE7F20_RTRMADP_3_GULF-QATAR-JAZEERA-1714943623.jpg?resize=96%2C96&quality=80)](/author/al_jazeera_staff_150119130629458)

By [Al Jazeera Staff](/author/al_jazeera_staff_150119130629458)

Published On 31 Oct 202631 Oct 2026

Police have arrested at least 48 people after protesters defied a warning not to attend a rally in London against the proscription of [Palestine Action](/news/2025/6/25/what-is-the-palestine-action-group-and-why-is-the-uk-banning-it), which is classified as a “terrorist” organisation under United Kingdom law.

Hundreds of people gathered outside the United States embassy on Saturday to oppose the ban, which came into effect in July last year under the government of then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

## Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

* list 1 of 3[Ethnic cleansing fears rise as Israel squeezes space in Gaza: UN](/news/2026/10/30/ethnic-cleansing-fears-rise-as-israel-squeezes-space-in-gaza-un)
* list 2 of 3[Fans voice support on final night of Macklemore’s ‘Free Palestine’ tour](/video/newsfeed/2026/10/30/fans-voice-support-on-final-night-of-macklemores-free-palestine-tour)
* list 3 of 3[A UN protection force must be urgently deployed to Palestine](/opinions/2026/10/31/a-un-protection-force-must-be-urgently-deployed-to-palestine)

end of list

The demonstration comes ahead of a [Supreme Court appeal](/video/newsfeed/2026/7/30/palestine-action-co-founder-wins-uk-supreme-court-appeal-bid) on Wednesday challenging the campaign group’s proscription.

“So far this afternoon, officers have arrested 48 people,” London’s Metropolitan Police said in a statement posted on X. “The majority of arrests have been for expressing support for a proscribed organisation. Officers remain at the scene and are continuing to make arrests.”

Responding to the police statement, Labour Party MP John McDonnell posted on X, saying someone protesting against the government’s decision to proscribe an organisation cannot be “automatically interpreted” as them supporting that organisation and “therefore committing an arrestable offence”.

He added that he believes the government “made the wrong decision in proscribing Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation”.

Saturday’s rally is the first mass protest against the proscription since Prime Minister Andy Burnham assumed office in July.

The decision to designate the group a “terrorist” organisation has triggered uproar among sections of British society, with critics arguing that it is part of a [wider crackdown](/news/2026/10/15/sally-rooney-withdraws-books-from-uk-over-palestine-action-support) aimed at silencing pro-Palestine voices. The proscription means Palestine Action has been added to a list of banned organisations that also includes al-Qaeda and ISIL (ISIS).

## UK ‘appeasing Trump and Israeli weapons companies’

Protesters also gathered outside the US consulate in Edinburgh, the Scottish capital. There have been no reports of arrests there.

Advertisement

Demonstrators in both London and Edinburgh could be seen holding placards reading “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action”.

Defend Our Juries, which organised the protests, said Saturday’s arrests took the total number of people detained for defying the Palestine Action ban to more than 4,000 since July 2025.

“It is truly dystopian that there have now been over 4,000 arrests under terror laws for peaceful vigils silently expressing opposition to genocide and support for the protest group Palestine Action,” a spokesperson for the group said, as reported by UK news agency Press Association.

“The ban on Palestine Action was straight out of [US President Donald] Trump’s playbook, so it’s fitting that this significant milestone has been reached on Halloween and outside the US embassy,” the spokesperson added, saying the proscription was about the UK government “appeasing Trump and the Israeli weapons companies that Palestine Action disrupted, not about any kind of terrorist threat”.

Felix Jakens, Amnesty International UK’s head of communications and campaigns, also called on the government to reverse Palestine Action’s proscription.

“The sight yet again of grandparents, teenagers and everyone in between being hauled into police vans for peacefully holding placards is a disgraceful attack on freedom of speech,” Jakens said in response to the arrests on Saturday.

“It’s past time for the government to drop the proscription of Palestine Action and reform our laws so that communities have more power to demonstrate on the issues they care about, not less.”

# Oasis help fundraise for London playing fields

![A group of young children in blue football kits and adults cheering together while a person takes their photograph on a sports pitch.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/8954/live/f484ad70-d464-11f1-ab12-eb0c94f5b382.jpg)

Business partners Audrey Carden and Eleanora Cunietti are organising the charity auction

**Oasis have donated VIP tickets to one of their UK reunion tour shows as part of a charity auction to help protect grassroots sport in London.**

The auction will raise money for the London Playing Fields Foundation, which operates seven grounds across six London boroughs.

The Gallagher brothers first supported the charity last summer through the "7 Shows, 7 Fields" campaign, which linked each of Oasis's seven Wembley Stadium concerts to a different playing field in the capital.

Alex Welsh, from the London Playing Fields Foundation, said: "I'm just so thankful that Liam and Noel played all that football on those fields in south Manchester, and they remembered the importance of them."

Welsh said a study at one of its grounds in Walthamstow found that the activities at the site generated at least £4.8m in savings to the public purse over a 12-month period.

He said this was achieved primarily by "reducing crime, anti-social behaviour, and improving health and wellbeing".

![Alex Welsh wearing a suit jacket and tie while standing outdoors on a grass playing field.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/466f/live/14803d10-d465-11f1-a701-fddedf244c16.jpg)

Alex Welsh said he was "thankful" to the Gallagher brothers

The new fundraiser is being organised by London-based interior design company Carden Cunietti.

Co-founder Audrey Carden said she and business partner Eleanora Cunietti had worked with Noel Gallagher and his manager for many years.

The campaign, called The Spring Clean, includes an online auction with between 75 and 100 donations from suppliers and other interior designers.

Among the items are a pair of VIP tickets to [Oasis's Knebworth House shows next year](/news/articles/c607lyyx3yvvo).

Carden said: "It's really important for people to be able to get outside in a city like London, where there's not a lot of outdoor space for children and adults as well."

The auction runs until 17 November and money raised will support the foundation.

# Gyles Brandreth shares seven habits that could help you live well to 100

From eating colourful foods to taking ‘exercise snacks’, the broadcaster shares his approach to longevity

![Avatar](https://s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/iya-news-prod.inyourarea.co.uk/2022/08/suruchi.jpg)
![](https://images-cropper-prod.inyourarea.co.uk/unsafe/700x394/smart/harvester-img-7876fde3d38948cd6d21a0205681b9d0.jpg)

###### *This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it[[**Learn more**](https://www.inyourarea.co.uk/news/information-on-affiliate-links/)]*

Living to 100 is one thing, but staying healthy, active and happy enough to enjoy those extra years is another. Broadcaster and author Gyles Brandreth, 78, believes seven simple habits could help people live longer and feel better as they age, from eating more colourful food to making time for friends and getting enough sleep.

The former Conservative MP, who regularly appears on Channel 4’s Countdown and ITV’s This Morning, has teamed up with his physiotherapist, Finola Burrell, to write The 7 Secrets of the Hundred-Year Life. Rather than promising a magic formula for longevity, the book explores everyday changes that could help people [protect their health](https://www.inyourarea.co.uk/news/tag/health) and make the most of later life.

“I think of myself as still quite young (bless me) and I am hoping to have snap in my celery for at least another 20 years,” Brandreth writes. “That’s why I have written this book. It’s a self-help book and it’s myself I am hoping to help!”

### YOUR HEALTH

Speaking to the Press Association, he said he had known many people who reached 100 and wanted to bring together the lessons he had learnt from them. “But actually how to have good living, because they want us to be 100 and just be sitting in a corner looking sad,” he said. “You want to live well to 100.”

Brandreth points to figures suggesting the number of centenarians worldwide has risen from around 23,000 a century ago to nearly 722,000 today, with that figure expected to reach four million by 2054. For anyone hoping to enjoy a longer, healthier life, he recommends seven habits.

### 1. Look on the bright side

Brandreth believes a positive outlook, a sense of purpose and something to look forward to can help people enjoy life for longer. He encourages people to stay curious, embrace change and find a passion that gives them a reason to get up in the morning.

“You need to look up and out rather than down and in. Busy people are happy people, and that’s why one of the golden rules is to cultivate a passion, have something you love doing, that makes you want to get up in the morning,” he says.

For Brandreth, that purpose is his work, but it could be a hobby, volunteering or learning a new skill. He also warns against becoming too set in your ways with age.

“Change is the salt and the soup of life,” he says. “As people get older, they find change difficult. People say don’t rock the boat, but in fact, a little gentle rocking does you good.”

![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/9b/37/9b37512a-c253-4f99-bb04-2eceff8988c5/content/images/2026/10/JS422523443--1-.jpg)

### 2. Eat a colourful diet and drink enough water

What you eat and drink can have a major impact on your health. Brandreth points to so-called Blue Zones - including Okinawa in Japan, Nicoya in Costa Rica and Sardinia in Italy - where people are known for living long, healthy lives.

Their diets feature [plant-based foods](https://www.inyourarea.co.uk/news/tag/inyourkitchen) such as vegetables, fruit, legumes and wholegrains, reflecting his recommendation to follow a [Mediterranean-style diet](https://www.inyourarea.co.uk/news/why-a-mediterranean-diet-could-be-the-secret-to-stronger-bones) with olive oil, moderate dairy and less red meat. “Getting the diet right is vital, and the essence of that is lots of colour on your plate,” he explains.

Research links plant-rich diets with better health outcomes, while regular consumption of processed and red meat is associated with a higher risk of early death. The book cites studies suggesting that replacing one daily serving of red meat with legumes, fish or chicken may reduce this risk by 7% to 19%.

Brandreth also stresses hydration, saying he has become more conscious of drinking water as he has got older. Daily fluid intake guidelines are around 2.7 litres for women and 3.7 litres for men, including fluids from food and other drinks, although needs vary.

“Just drink lots of water. It’s as simple as that,” he says. “Drinking water never interested me - now I’m a waterholic.”

### 3. Make time to breathe properly

Breathing happens automatically, but Brandreth believes paying attention to it can be a useful way to relax and manage stress. He highlights techniques such as diaphragmatic breathing, box breathing and nasal breathing as ways to help people slow down and focus on the present.

While they cannot guarantee a longer life, these [simple exercises](https://www.inyourarea.co.uk/news/tag/exercise) can be incorporated into daily routines without special equipment or a gym membership.

![](https://storage.ghost.io/c/9b/37/9b37512a-c253-4f99-bb04-2eceff8988c5/content/images/2026/10/JS422523441--1-.jpg)

### 4. Stay connected with other people

Brandreth says staying connected with friends, family and the wider community is vital to healthy ageing, as loneliness and social isolation are linked to poorer health and earlier death. [His book cites](https://fave.co/47xiWyq) a Chinese study associating isolation and loneliness with a four-to-five-year reduction in life expectancy for men, while isolation alone was linked to a three-year reduction for women.

“To live to 100, staying socially engaged is as essential as exercise, nutrition, sleep and purpose,” he says. “Communicating is vital - you won’t live to be 100 if you’re on your own.” Meeting friends, joining clubs and making regular phone calls can all help maintain social connections.

### 5. Give sleep the attention it deserves

Brandreth says good-quality sleep is vital for healthy ageing, with poor sleep linked to a range of health problems. He recommends getting natural daylight within an hour of waking, limiting bright light and digital devices before bed, and keeping sleep, wake and meal times consistent.

He explains that inadequate sleep can affect the body at a cellular level and says a regular lifestyle can make a difference. “Sleep is key - you can’t survive without sleep. Getting into a way of life that’s regular and ordered is good,” he says.

### 6. Keep moving - even in short bursts

Brandreth admits he has never enjoyed traditional exercise, but says staying active is important as people get older. Rather than following an intense fitness routine, he recommends finding simple ways to move more throughout the day.

“I don’t like exercise. I am not interested in exercise. But you do need to keep moving, and it needn’t be depressing,” he says. His ‘exercise snacks’ include short bursts of activity, such as walking, taking the stairs or moving between tasks. Brandreth has also started working with a personal trainer and trying boxing, which he says has helped him lose a stone.

“I am now doing the exercise, so I’ve lost a stone. I’m topping the exercise snacks up with a personal trainer, so I’m knocking 80 and I’ve started boxing, which is quite fun,” he says.

His message is that staying active need not mean spending hours exercising or following a demanding fitness plan.

### 7. Keep it simple and consistent

Brandreth’s final tip is not to get overwhelmed by longevity advice, but to focus on small, sustainable habits that can be repeated every day. “Longevity isn’t achieved through extreme diets or sporadic bursts of intense exercise that are not sustainable throughout the decades, but rather through the cumulative, positive effects of simple repeated actions,” he explains.

“So keeping busy, looking up, looking out, staying happy, staying hydrated, eating colourful food, and taking exercise snacks is all you need, and you’ll live to be 100,” Brandreth says.

*The* [*7 Secrets of the Hundred-Year Life by Gyles Brandreth and Finola Burrell*](https://fave.co/47xiWyq) *is published by Short Books and is priced at £16.99.*

### 🌿 Books to help you live a longer, healthier life

*This article contains affiliate links, and we may receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. [Learn more](https://www.inyourarea.co.uk/news/information-on-affiliate-links/).*

Want to make the most of the years ahead? From the everyday habits of the world's longest-living communities to the science of healthy ageing, these books offer ideas and practical advice on living well for longer.

🌍 **Best for discovering the secrets of longevity:** [The Blue Zones Secrets for Living Longer by Dan Buettner](https://fave.co/4e0PCE8) National Geographic explorer Dan Buettner investigates communities where people tend to live longer, healthier lives. Drawing on his research into places including Okinawa in Japan and Sardinia in Italy, the book explores the role of natural movement, plant-based eating, purpose and strong social connections. **Price: £25.99**

🥗 **Best for exploring the link between food and ageing:** [The Longevity Diet by Dr Valter Longo](https://fave.co/4BsiEXk) This guide examines how eating habits may affect health as we age, drawing on research into nutrition, fasting and age-related disease. It offers a food-focused approach for readers interested in making longer-term changes to support their health. **Price: £16.14**

❤️ **Best for understanding why relationships matter:** [The Good Life by Robert Waldinger and Marc Schulz](https://fave.co/4knkoL8) Based on the Harvard Study of Adult Development, this book explores what decades of research can tell us about happiness and wellbeing. It puts relationships, connection and the quality of our everyday lives at the heart of the discussion, making it a good choice for anyone looking beyond diet and exercise. **Price: £14.24**

🧠 **Best for a fresh perspective on a longer life:** [The 100-Year Life by Lynda Gratton and Andrew J Scott](https://fave.co/3WbJToQ) What happens when living to 100 becomes more common? This book considers how longer lives could change the way we approach work, money, education and relationships, helping readers think about how to make different stages of life more fulfilling. **Price: £11.69**

# Philips Sonicare introduces AI toothbrush designed to transform daily brushing habits

**Philips’ new AI toothbrush uses real-time personalised guidance to help patients improve their brushing technique, remove more plaque and develop healthier oral care habits between dental appointments.**

Good oral health has never been more important. Research increasingly links oral health with wider wellbeing, including cardiovascular disease, diabetes and cognitive health, yet many patients still struggle to know whether they’re brushing effectively between dental appointments.

Philips has found a way to remedy this and effect significant behavioural change with the launch of its most advanced electric toothbrush to date. The new **Next-Generation DiamondClean 9900 Prestige** is the brand’s first toothbrush to combine on-device artificial intelligence and real-time personalised brushing guidance to help users achieve more complete plaque removal and healthier gums.

Unlike conventional electric toothbrushes, the 9900 Prestige provides live coaching during every brushing session. An on-device 12-segment Mouth Map highlights areas which have been missed – in real time – before confirming a complete clean, whilst a light ring alerts users if they’re applying too much pressure or scrubbing. Combined with Philips’ SenseIQ technology, the toothbrush is designed to help remove up to 20 times more plaque and deliver up to 15 times healthier gums compared with manual brushing.

In these videos a number of leading dental professionals explain the significance of the new technological advances Philips has introduced in its next generation brush and the implications for the patients:

## AI toothbrush technology brings professional guidance into the home

The importance of improving daily brushing habits extends far beyond the mouth. Professor Ian Chapple explains: ‘We’re no longer treating the mouth simply to save teeth, we’re protecting overall health.’

Helping patients change long-established habits is one of the greatest challenges facing dental professionals. Dental Hygienist Anna Middleton believes technology which provides visual feedback could be the missing link bridging the gap between advice given in the surgery and behaviour at home.

She says: ‘The problem usually isn’t that patients aren’t brushing, it’s that they’re not brushing effectively,’ she explains. ‘We’re not standing beside our patients every morning and every evening, but this technology almost can.’

## How an AI toothbrush can improve daily brushing habits

One of the key innovations is Smart Coverage Feedback, which guides users back to areas they’ve missed before they finish brushing, reinforcing better habits every day.

The new toothbrush also tackles another common issue seen in dental practices: brushing too hard. Dr Chinwe Akuonu says excessive scrubbing can contribute to gum recession, tooth wear and sensitivity.

‘Many patients think scrubbing harder means cleaning better, but the opposite is true,’ she says. ‘It’s a simple feature, but it drives meaningful behavioural change.’

For patients with dental implants, intelligent pressure sensing may offer additional benefits. As Dr Nilesh Parmar notes, implants require meticulous home care to remain healthy.

He states: ‘Great oral health isn’t about brushing harder, it’s about brushing smarter,’ and adds, ‘The technology removes much of the guesswork.’

For him the stand outs of the new brush are the real-time pressure feedback and Mouth Map which can help patients clean thoroughly while avoiding unnecessary force around delicate implant tissues.

## Prevention and patient empowerment

For Dr Ben Atkins, the launch reflects a broader shift towards prevention and patient empowerment.

‘Behaviour change is the biggest challenge in dentistry,’ he says. ‘The beauty of the new Sonicare brush is that it supports patients every day, even when I’m not there.’

He believes technology should simplify oral care rather than complicate it, helping patients build healthier routines between appointments.

The launch of the Next-Generation DiamondClean 9900 Prestige builds on Philips Sonicare’s wider next-generation portfolio and reflects growing interest in personalised oral healthcare powered by intelligent technology. By combining AI-driven coaching with clinically proven sonic cleaning, Philips hopes to give both dental professionals and patients greater confidence that brushing at home is as effective as possible.

As dentistry increasingly focuses on prevention rather than treatment, technologies that provide real-time guidance could play an important role in improving everyday oral health, one brushing session at a time.

[Experience Next-Generation DiamondClean for yourself, and request a trial handle.](https://www.philips.co.uk/c-m-pe/dental-professionals#_sales_form)

# 5 science-backed simple daily habits to keep your blood pressure under control

They're simple habits with huge health benefits

By [Anna Bartter](/uk/author/470344/anna-bartter/)

## Jump to:

* [5 simple daily habits to keep your blood pressure under control](#5-simple-daily-habits-to-keep-your-blood-pressure-under-control)

If you’re fit and healthy, chances are you’ve given little (if any) thought to your blood pressure – aside, perhaps, from the occasional routine GP check. But according to a [recent study](https://bmjpublichealth.bmj.com/content/4/3/e004815) conducted by researchers at the University of Oxford, millions of us could be living with high blood pressure, increasing our risk of disease and premature death.

And the scariest part? We might have absolutely no idea. According to the research, two-thirds of those with high blood pressure are unaware of their diagnosis.

'The biggest problem with hypertension is that it usually causes zero symptoms,' says GP and co-founder of [Coyne Medical](https://coynemedical.com/), Dr Lucy Hooper. 'You can feel completely well while carrying high blood pressure for years, even though it is increasing your risk of heart disease, kidney disease and serious illness such as a heart attack or a stroke.'

The good news, though, is that there’s a range of easy everyday habits we can all adopt to help keep blood pressure under control. Alongside regular monitoring of your blood pressure, these steps should help to keep your risk of blood pressure-related conditions to a minimum.

'While we can’t change your genetics or your family history, we can effectively lower your blood pressure,' notes Dr Hooper. 'High blood pressure is one of the most important risk factors for cardiovascular disease that we can modify via lifestyle interventions.'

## 5 simple daily habits to keep your blood pressure under control

## **1. Brisk walking**

It’s well established that a daily walk is one of the simplest ways to boost both mental and physical wellbeing; there’s a wealth of science to back it up, too. [Studies](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10643563/) show that it is effective in decreasing our risk of developing cardiovascular disease, as well as boosting longevity and mental wellbeing, too.

## What to Read Next

'One of the best things you can do for lowering blood pressure is aim for 30 minutes of brisk walking five days a week,' shares GP and founder of [Align](https://drbaileyalign.co.uk/), Dr Flora Bailey. 'You should feel slightly out of breath but still be able to hold a conversation. If that feels like too much, start with 10-minute walks and build up gradually.'

## **2. Break up sedentary time**

But a daily walk won’t cut it if you spend the rest of the day sitting down, experts warn.

'Get moving every hour,' advises Dr Nadia Ahmad, GP and founder of [The Weight Care Clinic](https://theweightcareclinic.com/). 'If you work at a desk, try standing up and walking around for three to five minutes every hour.

'Long periods of sitting are associated with poorer cardiovascular health. Breaking up sedentary time adds movement throughout the day, although it shouldn’t replace regular exercise.'

## **3. Eat** a DASH diet

'A DASH diet is Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension diet,' explains Dr Luke Powles, associate clinical director at [Bupa Health Clinics](https://www.bupa.co.uk/health/payg). 'This is a diet which focuses on veg, fruit and whole grains. It involves fat-free or low-fat dairy products, fish, poultry, beans and nuts. The diet limits sugar, saturated fats such as fatty meats and food high in salt. The DASH diet helps to lower blood pressure by lowering the amount of sodium in your diet and promoting good cholesterol.'

![mind diet foods](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/mind-diet-foods-669654f175f0a.png?crop=1.00xw:0.752xh;0,0.0561xh&resize=980:* "mind diet foods")

getty

## **4. Wall squats**

A [new study](https://bmjopensem.bmj.com/content/12/3/e003172) has revealed a simple exercise that could help to keep our blood pressure in check: the humble wall squat. Even performed as little as just once or twice a week, isometric training (exercise which involve static contractions of muscles, like a wall squat) has been shown to reduce systolic blood pressure – and the new research shows that it can help us to maintain this reduction, too.

Over the course of eight weeks, 100 adults were randomly assigned to one of five groups. One of the groups was a control group, while the other four groups were assigned a four-week at-home exercise program which consisted of four wall squat holds per session, with two minutes of seated recovery between each hold. They completed these sessions three times a week.

After those four weeks, the groups were given different schedules. One continued as normal, while the others reduced their training frequency. While those who continued as normal experienced the greatest reduction in blood pressure, those who did one or two sessions a week still maintained significant reductions in their blood pressure, showing that even short wall squat sessions can make a difference.

'Wall squats are a great example of an isometric exercise,' explains personal trainer [Anwen Davies](https://www.forza.com/uk/author/anwen-davies). 'According to research, isometric training has the largest effect on blood pressure of any training type – it’s also very efficient in terms of time usage. Try a fifteen-minute session, including rests, around three times a week.'

## **5. Reduce stress**

We know: easier said than done. But focusing on stress reduction can be a powerful tool in treating (and preventing) hypertension.

'Too much stress can raise your blood pressure,' agrees Dr Powles. 'Too much stress can also lead to bad habits such as, eating unhealthily, smoking or consuming too much alcohol. It’s completely normal to feel stressed, worried or anxious, but there’s lots of ways to keep your stress at bay.

'Mindfulness, speaking to loved ones (whether it’s virtually or face-to-face) or making lists to organise your thoughts can all help; it’s important to find what works for you.'

# 2026: The new golden age of horror films?

With most of the world on fire you might think the last thing people want to see is a horror film.

But in fact the opposite is the case – with 2026 proving to be a new golden age for horror.

Scary movies are taking millions at the box office, as well as picking up nominations for all the top awards. Clearly the Spooky season isn’t just for Halloween. And a warning, there are scares and screaming right from the start of this report.

# In praise of halloween classics

**Vivienne Howells** explores the enduring appeal of horror classics

![](/images/dyn/WGqMwettbas/store/600/0/55779.jpg)

by Vivienne Howells

Saturday October 31 2026, 4:55pm

“What’s your favourite scary movie?” So goes the haunting question Ghostface poses to his victims in the *Scream* franchise. And, in the shadow of Halloween, I pose the same question to you. Which films do you return to year after year? What frightens you most? And, most importantly, what will you be watching this Halloweekend?

This year has seen something of a resurgence in horror. Although released in May rather than October, two new icons of the genre have emerged: *Backrooms* and *Obsession*. While I enjoyed both, I find that the films we return to on the spooky, wintry weekends leading up to Halloween are often the originals.

The 1960s marked a shift in the horror genre. Where audiences in the 1950s could expect gruesome violence, monsters and fantastical creatures, the following decade ushered in a turn towards the human and the real. Hitchcock’s 1960 psychological thriller *Psycho* is widely credited with spearheading this transition. Its villain (spoilers!) is not an alien creature beyond the audience’s conception, but the seemingly unassuming and disarming motel proprietor, Norman Bates. By stripping horror of its fantastical elements and relocating fear in recognisable figures, Hitchcock paved the way for the genre’s future. This shift found its expression in the 1970s classics *Halloween* and *The Shining*, whose horrors lie firmly in human evil. Both pre-2000, pre-CGI cult classics, they frighten me far more than any modern adaptation could.

“Pre-CGI cult classics frighten me far more than any modern adaptation could”

There is something far more unsettling about the suggestion that the familiar might conceal something deeply sinister than there is in the graphic violence and CGI monsters that populate so many contemporary horror releases. John Carpenter’s 1978 classic *Halloween* embodies precisely this danger: the evil lurking beneath an otherwise ordinary, even comforting, exterior.

Set on Halloween night in the fictional town of Haddonfield, Illinois, the film follows the return of Michael Myers, who murdered his older sister fifteen years earlier, when he was just six years old. Having escaped from a psychiatric institution, Myers returns to his hometown on the anniversary of his first act of violence. Dr Loomis, his former psychiatrist, recognises the danger he poses, but nobody else seems to share his concern. The film follows Laurie Strode, played by a young Jamie Lee Curtis in her screen debut, as Myers stalks her and her friends, picking them off one by one. Dressed in overalls and an expressionless mask, he is a disturbingly ordinary figure.

On the surface, *Halloween* is deceptively mild. Haddonfield’s suburban setting, seasonal festivities and familiar teenage dramas of boyfriends and friendships initially suggest a harmless portrait of an all-American town. But darkness lurks beneath this suburban tranquillity. The film opens with Myers murdering his sister in a handheld sequence, viewed through the eyeholes of the mask he will wear throughout the film. This unsettling alignment of the audience’s perspective with that of the killer brings the violence uncomfortably close. The revelation that the murderer is a six-year-old boy, the younger brother of his victim, further undermines any comfort we might have found in the charming suburban setting. From its opening moments, *Halloween* presents the corruption of the family home and domestic life through the eyes of a killer. We are off-kilter from the very beginning.

“Illinois suburbs really are a horror movie”

As one Letterboxd user puts it: “Illinois suburbs really are a horror movie”. Though glib, the comment inadvertently captures the film’s central horror. Haddonfield is not the suburban idyll it first appears to be. Its violence is embedded in the town’s history, resurfacing with Myers’ return. Evil is no longer something unusual or distant; it has become part of the familiar.

Stanley Kubrick’s *The Shining* achieves a similar effect through defamiliarisation. Described in my Letterboxd research as a “chilling descent into […] domestic terror”, Kubrick’s 1980 masterpiece follows the Torrance family as they spend the winter caring for the isolated Overlook Hotel. It would be remiss to discuss this film without acknowledging Kubrick’s extraordinary cinematography. *The Shining* is a visual jewel of colour and pattern: the hotel’s geometric carpets, the snowy expanse of the maze, the mint-green and yellow bathrooms, and the river of blood pouring from the lifts all contribute to its ethereal, terrifying atmosphere. Yet this visual splendour is undercut by a deeply unsettling psychological narrative of insanity and domestic violence.

READ MORE

![Mountain View](https://www.varsity.co.uk/images/dyn/cmpse-Y0P2o/store/1200/0/55581.jpg)

American Dream or American Nightmare?

During their stay, the Torrances are haunted by visions. Young Danny sees the ghostly Grady twins and a succession of disturbing figures; Jack encounters a phantom bartender and a ballroom full of guests; Wendy witnesses a man in a bear costume. These supernatural encounters culminate in Jack’s descent into madness and his attempt to murder his wife and son. After a prolonged pursuit through the hotel and its grounds, Wendy and Danny escape, while Jack freezes to death in the maze. But the final image of the film complicates this apparent resolution: a photograph reveals Jack among the guests of the Overlook in 1921. Although the film toys with the supernatural and the possibility of reincarnation, its most disturbing horror remains profoundly human. Beneath the ghosts and spectral apparitions lies a harrowing study of domestic violence, paranoia and the disintegration of a family.

What both films share is the devil you know. Their villains are not incomprehensible monsters, detached from the world we inhabit. They are recognisable figures: brother, father, neighbour. Michael Myers emerges from the familiar streets of suburbia; Jack Torrance turns the family home, however temporary, into a site of terror. Perhaps this is why we return to *Halloween* and *The Shining* year after year. They remind us that evil does not always announce itself. Sometimes, it is already at home. Don’t look behind you.

We are therefore almost entirely reliant on advertising for funding and we expect to have a tough few months and years ahead.

In spite of this situation, we are going to look at inventive ways to look at serving our readership with digital content and of course in print too!

resource.title: 19 Best Non-Scary Films You Can Stream At Home Now To Get In The Halloween Spirit
resource.content:
# 19 Best Non-Scary Halloween Films To Get In The Spooky Spirit

Our Halloween watchlist is all treats with no tricks – and won't give you nightmares.

![Daniel Welsh](https://img.huffingtonpost.com/asset/63b5b92c2400001e009957e9.jpg?ops=100_100)

Entertainment Editor

With the peak of spooky season in sight, it’s time to finally get your [Halloween](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/halloween/) watchlist together.

For many, that’ll mean diving into the horror vault to find something suitably scary.

But, if you’re someone for whom your typical horror movie requires a 30-minute pep talk beforehand, multiple tea breaks midway through, and a one-hour cool-down afterwards, picking something to watch on Halloween can be… well… a bit of a frightful task.

![A selection of the non-scary Halloween films streaming this spooky season](https://img.huffingtonpost.com/asset/6ae0e22e1400001b8ae0176e.jpg?cache=Ub2Leqp2dv&ops=scalefit_720_noupscale)

That’s why we’ve put together this no-tricks, all-treats list of Halloween-friendly movies that still pack in a spooky thrill, without haunting your nightmares for days afterwards.

You’re welcome…

## **Hocus Pocus**

[Bette Midler](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/bette-midler/), [Sarah Jessica Parker](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/sarah-jessica-parker/) and [Kathy Najimy](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/kathy-najimy/) chewing the scenery as a coven in this family-friendly Halloween treat is camp enough as a concept, but when you throw the mix of costumes, wigs and musical numbers into the witches’ brew it just makes it even more irresistible.

[Hocus Pocus](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/hocus-pocus/)’ legacy feels even more well-earned when you factor in that it [initially underperformed at the box office](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/i-just-learned-the-origins-of-hocus-pocus-and-its-absolutely-adorable_uk_66e99bb2e4b06998fbed3076), but eventually found a cult audience among home viewers, leading to it becoming valuable property for Disney at this time of year ([let’s just not talk about that 2022 sequel](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/hocus-pocus-sequel-receives-mixed-reviews-from-critics_uk_6336c34de4b0e376dbf5e745), alright?).

**Stream it on:** Disney+

## **Practical Magic**

[Practical Magic](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/../../../news/practical-magic/) is what happens if you mix the autumnal cosiness of Gilmore Girls, the modern witchy vibes of The Craft and the sheer Oscar-winning acting greatness of [Nicole Kidman](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/../../../news/nicole-kidman/) and [Sandra Bullock](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/../../../news/sandra-bullock/).

Weirdly, it sort of came and went when it was first released in the late 1990s, but eventually went on to become a bona fide cult classic, to the point it spawned a long-awaited sequel reuniting almost all of its cast earlier this year.

But let’s face it, the original is always going to be the best.

**Stream it on:** Netflix, Amazon Prime Video and Now

## **Addams Family Values**

Sorry, [Jenna Ortega](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/jenna-ortega/), but Christina Ricci is forever the true Wednesday Addams in our eyes.

One of those few sequels that’s actually better than the original, Addams Family Values puts your usual domestic comedy through a twisted lens and the results are not just hilarious, but also suspenseful, spooky, sexy and surprisingly heartwarming.

If you’ve still not treated yourself to this movie, consider the fact it’s currently available on *three*different UK streaming services as your indication to finally see what the fuss is all about.

**Stream it on:** Now, Paramount+ and Amazon Prime Video.

## **The Witches**

Forget Lady Gaga, Heidi Klum and even Jenna Ortega – Addams Family Values *and* The Witches prove that the Queen of Halloween title still belongs to Anjelica Huston.

If you’ve not watched The Witches since childhood and you’re curious as to whether it’s still deeply unsettling despite its alleged “family friendly” label, we’re here to assure you that, yes, it absolutely is.

**Stream it on:** Amazon Prime Video, Now and HBO Max

## **The Rocky Horror Picture Show**

This cult classic send-up of Hollywood B-movies is a tale as old as time.

Boy meets girl. Boy proposes to girl. Boy heads out to share the happy news with their old college professor. Boy breaks down at the side of the road and seeks shelter in an old castle inhabited by a cross-dressing alien who seduces both of them in a bid to teach the world about indulging in all of life’s pleasures.

It’s just a jump to the left!

**Stream it on:** Disney+

## **The Nightmare Before Christmas**

Come on, it wouldn’t be Halloween without a bit of [Tim Burton](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/tim-burton/), would it? When it comes to setting the scene at this time of year, opening numbers don’t come any more perfectly than This Is Halloween, and who doesn’t love a film where both the hero and the villain are deliciously spooky characters?

[If you think](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/the-director-settled-the-debate-of-whether-nightmare-before-christmas-is-a-halloween-film_uk_670d2295e4b0c5b8c0aebc98) this one is more of an alternative Christmas movie than an on-brand Halloween one, cool. Good for you, see you in December. For everyone else, happy streaming!

**Stream it on:** Disney+

## **Coraline**

Another offering from Nightmare Before Christmas director Henry Selick that’s perfect for spooky season is Coraline, in which the titular teenager stumbles upon a secret world while home alone that she quickly discovers is more sinister than it first appears.

The stop-motion movie has gained a loyal cult following since its release in 2009, and is now [considered a game-changer within the world of animation](https://collider.com/best-animated-movies-of-the-21st-century/).

**Stream it on:** ITVX and Amazon Prime Video

## **KPop Demon Hunters**

Already onto your millionth stream of Golden and Soda Pop, despite [KPop Demon Hunters](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/../../../news/kpop-demon-hunters/) coming out a year ago? Us too! But come on, it’s Halloween... why not make it a million and one?

**Stream it on:** Netflix

## **Ghostbusters**

This game-changing supernatural comedy spawned a thousand spin-offs, sequels and reboots but as with so many franchises, it’s pretty hard to improve on the original, isn’t it?

Good luck getting that iconic theme tune out of your head before Bonfire Night, though…

**Stream it on:** Now

## **Beetlejuice**

Tim Burton was truly firing on all cylinders when he put together 1988’s original film Beetlejuice, earning his title as prince of weirdos the world over.

Michael Keaton is having the time of his life as the film’s central anti-hero, leading an all-star cast that includes the late, great Catherine O’Hara, Geena Davis, Alec Baldwin and, of course, Winona Ryder in one of her own earliest oddball roles.

Never more appropriate a watch than on Halloween, the film boasts some of the most memorable, imaginative and truly ridiculous sequences in Tim Burton’s entire career.

**Stream it on:** Now, HBO Max and Amazon Prime Video

## **Corpse Bride**

While we’re celebrating Tim Burton’s oeuvre, this month Corpse Bride is celebrating its 20th anniversary, so what could be a more ideal moment to revisit this dark and imaginative animated musical?

**Stream it on:** Now, HBO Max and Amazon Prime Video

## **Labyrinth**

Labyrinth served as an ambitious collaboration between Jim Henson, George Lucas and David Bowie, which is how it manages to incorporate expansive set-pieces, irreverent humour and a couple of Bowie bops into what’s otherwise, let’s be frank, a deeply weird fantasy set-up.

**Stream it on:** ITVX, Amazon Prime Video and Plex

## **The Adventures Of Ichabod And Mr Toad**

You might be wondering exactly what Toad of Toad Hall and The Wind In The Willows have to do with Halloween. And the answer to that question is... nothing at all!

However, it’s the second half of this early-years [Disney](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/disney/) package film we’d encourage you to watch this spooky season, as it tells the story of The Legend Of Sleepy Hollow.

And while people are quick to highlight the nightmare fuel Disney provided us with in The Black Cauldron, Pinocchio and Snow White, among others, trust us when we say you’re not quite ready for how eerie this oft-overlooked offering from the studio gets, either.

**Stream it on:** Disney+

## **It’s The Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown**

Already a seasonal staple across the pond, this Peanuts Halloween special was finally available to stream in the UK for Apple TV+ users in the last few years.

Often celebrated as the pinnacle of Charlie Brown, Snoopy and co’s small-screen offerings, this 25-minute episode is utterly charming and guaranteed to appeal to viewers of all ages.

**Stream it on:** Apple TV+

## **Muppets Haunted Mansion**

Off the back of Pirates Of The Caribbean’s success, Disney has tried several times to adapt other park attractions for the big screen, including Jungle Cruise and Tomorrowland.

After past iterations of The Haunted Mansion were met with varying levels of success, who could have guessed that all Disney would need to really bring the brand to life would be chucking the [Muppets](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/the-muppets/) into the mix?

Yes, after dominating the festive season for the last few decades, the Muppets turned their attention to Halloween in 2021, and we have to say the results worked surprisingly well.

**Stream it on:** Disney+

## **Scooby-Doo**

A film that has aged like a fine wine, this live-action reimagining of the classic Scooby-Doo cartoons boasts an impressive all-star cast, multi-layered humour that all generations can appreciate, gorgeous costumes and an absolute banger of a soundtrack thanks to Allstars’ Things That Go Bump In The Night.

If it’s been long enough now that you don’t instinctively know every twist and turn as it comes, we can’t recommend giving this one a stream enough (and the oft-overlooked sequel Monsters Unleashed is also available, too, if you wanted to make it a double feature).

**Stream it on:** Netflix, Amazon Prime Video and Disney+

## **Hotel Transylvania**

A guaranteed hit if you have sensitive or younger viewers you need to keep entertained for an hour or two this Halloween, but at the very least, Hotel Transylvania makes for a fun guessing game as you try to work out which celebs on the A-list cast have lent their voice to each of the spooky characters.

**Stream it on:** ITX, Amazon Prime Video and Now

## **Twilight**

Taking Gilmore Girls and pumpkin spice in general out of the equation, nothing says autumn quite like revisiting Bella and Edward’s infamous love story, right?

And, much like Pringles, even if you think you can just stop at one – Disney+ has the entire Twilight saga available to stream, so good luck not hitting “continue watching” when those credits start rolling and you find yourself in need of another immediate nostalgia hit…

**Stream it on:** ITVX and Netflix

## **Mean Girls**

No, [Mean Girls](https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/news/mean-girls/) probably isn’t your traditional “Halloween film”, but its Halloween party section features so many iconic moments – “I’m a mouse, duh!”, “why do you look so scary?!” “It’s Halloween!”, “yeah, but he’s my first cousin…” – we’ve included it on this list regardless.

Besides, who actually needs an excuse to watch Mean Girls? See you again in December when we’re ready to do the Jingle Bell Rock with the Plastics…

**Stream it on:** Paramount+, Netflix and Amazon Prime Video

![Manchester Evening News](/nav-web-static/main-87bac421972ba8a3b4cb8982cfa404878ba82c15/public/assets/men/logos/masthead-men-default.svg "Manchester Evening News: Number one for news, opinion, sport & celebrity news")

# The five scariest films available to stream for free in the UK this Halloween

## Both the BBC and ITV have lots of horror gems for you to choose from this year

![](https://i2-prod.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/article31288923.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200f/0_Get-Out.jpg)

Daniel Kaluuya starred in Jordan Peele's directorial debut Get Out(Image: Blumhouse Productions)

Halloween is finally here, which means it’s time to start scanning the streaming services to find the perfect horror movie to watch for your spooky night in.

With the nights getting darker, the temperatures. beginning to plummet and the haunted [Christmas](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/christmas) ads already playing on the telly, nothing beats getting a scare from the comfort of your own home.

While some people would prefer to get dressed up and go on a night out, October 31 is a day that [movie](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/film) buffs cherish with all of their hearts. Just make sure to keep the light on and that your cupboards are full of snacks.

***[Click here](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/newsletter-preference-centre/?view=Solus&mailingListId=b8052254-66af-41f3-9dae-7bbb0e3391c6&utm_source=solusarticle) to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter***

Rather than spending hours on end trying to find the perfect horror film, we’ve picked out a number of flicks that may leave you sleeping with the light on for a few nights. Best of all, they’re all streaming for free if you have a TV licence.

## **Get Out (BBC iPlayer)**

![](https://i2-prod.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/article31288924.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/0_Get-Out-2.jpg)

The film in question saw Daniel Kaluuya become a household name

No horror movie has made the cultural impact like Get Out has in such a short period of time. Directed by former comedian [Jordan Peele](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/tv/horror-movie-uk-actor-tv-31544715), the film tells the story of a man (Daniel Kaluuya) whose worst fears come true at his girlfriend’s parents’ house during a weekend getaway.

While the horror genre often focuses on gore, there’s a lot to be said that the tension of Get Out is fuelled mostly on psychological scares. Nominated for four Oscars, Get Out’s reputation has only grown stronger over the years.

## **Halloween (BBC iPlayer)**

![](https://i2-prod.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/article34824157.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/1_ACR_Films131022_01.jpg)

Michael Myers is one of cinema's scariest bad guys(Image: Press Association Images)

When it comes to [Halloween](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/all-about/halloween?pageNumber=6) films, there’s few as suitable for the evening than John Carpenter’s 1978 masterpiece. Introducing both Michael Myers and Jamie Lee Curtis to the world, it still packs one hell of a punch nearly 50 years after its release.

***Don't let an algorithm decide what Manchester news you see - [click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=manchestereveningnews.co.uk)***

For those who haven’t seen it, Halloween follows escaped mental patient Michael Myers, who was committed to a mental institution for murdering his teenage sister on Halloween in the town of Haddonfield. 15 years later, he returns to stalk teenage babysitter Laurie Strode (Curtis) and her friends while his psychiatrist Dr. Samuel Loomis (Donald Pleasence) pursues him.

The sequels are a bit hit or miss, or in the case of Halloween: Resurrection an abomination to cinema, so stick with the original even if you’ve watched it a million times before.

## **The Substance (BBC iPlayer)**

![Demi Moore looks into the mirror in a still from body horror movie The Substance](https://i2-prod.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/article30344874.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/3_the-substance.jpg)

Demi Moore plays Elisabeth Sparkle in The Substance(Image: Mubi)

Body horror is one of the horror genre’s most underrated aspects of horror, giving us films including The Fly, The Thing and Under the Skin. When it comes to the 2020s, The Substance is body horror’s crowning achievement.

Released in 2024, the film was written and directed by French auteur Coralie Fargeat. It follows a fading celebrity (Demi Moore) who is fired by her producer (Dennis Quaid) due to her age and uses a black market drug that creates a younger woman (Margaret Qualley) with unexpected side effects.

After years spent in supporting roles, it was a delight seeing Moore showcase why she was one of the most famous people in the world in the 1990s. Playing the younger version of Moore, Qualley is just as good.

Not only stomach churning with its imagery, [The Substance](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/tv/horror-film-pushes-fans-absolute-30345259) is an essential tale in a world where more and more people feel like they need cosmetic surgery to feel at peace with their looks.

## **The Babadook (ITVX)**

![The Babadook](https://i2-prod.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/article30085176.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/0_The-Babadook-1.jpg)

The Babadook(Image: UMBRELLA ENTERTAINMENT)

Recent years have seen a wave of indie horror films taking over the nation. Part of the magic of living in the streaming age is that we have the power to be scared by projects from all over the world. It could be argued that The Babadook kick started this trend.

The 2014 Australian psychological horror film, written and directed by Jennifer Kent in her feature directorial debut, follows a widowed single mother who, with her son, must confront a mysterious humanoid monster in their home.

It may not be as violent as a slasher film, yet the amount of terror found inside its 94 runtime is immense. Without it, we may not have had other Australian gems such as [Talk To Me](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/uk-news/new-horror-movie-talk-branded-27391298), Relic or Little Monsters.

## **It Follows (ITVX)**

![](https://i2-prod.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/article34824178.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/1_DBR_SCU_260215filmclip_10.jpg)

(Image: Shared Content Unit)

Earlier in the year, [The End of Oak Street](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/whats-on/film-news/film-fans-admit-i-not-33669887) came from director David Robert Mitchell. If you watched the family dinosaur film, you may be surprised to learn that Mitchell made his name with a supernatural horror film.

Starring Longlegs’ Maika Monroe, 2014’s It Follows tells the story of a young woman who is pursued by a supernatural entity. In a genius twist, it turns out that the only way to get the entity to leave you alone is by sleeping with another person.

If you find out you love the film, you’ll be delighted to know that a long-rumoured sequel, They Follow, was filmed earlier this year and set to come out in the next 12 months.

# The 15 most terrifying horror films set at Halloween and where to watch them

![Rebecca Sayce](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/0_FwkxVk_400x400-379f.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=400&resize=200,200&zoom=1)
![The 15 most terrifying horror films set at Halloween and where to watch them getty/ metro](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/SEI_318272463-b5d0.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646)

Unless you’re a [pagan](https://metro.co.uk/2015/01/25/why-we-should-start-taking-paganism-seriously-5008750/#:~:text=You're%20Pagan%20but%20you%20don't%20know%20it&text=If%20you%20have%20ever%20dressed,that%20emanated%20from%20their%20beliefs.) who celebrates [Halloween](https://metro.co.uk/tag/halloween/) with rituals or attempting to commune with the dead, the occasion is probably [mostly just about sweets](https://metro.co.uk/2017/10/14/why-do-we-celebrate-halloween-and-where-does-halloween-come-from-6999399/#:~:text=Samhain%20is%20a%20Celtic%20pagan,and%20going%20to%20Halloween%20parties.), isn’t it?

Many of us will be distracted on October 31, ensuring that the plastic cauldron outside our front door is adequately stocked to guarantee that next door’s kids don’t flip out during a mad sugar rush and kick over our favourite plant pot or ram a fistful of Haribo Starmix up our car’s exhaust pipe.

When we’re not doing that, Halloween’s a time for getting creeped out by [horror films](https://metro.co.uk/tag/horror-movies/).

And right now, there are a hellishly innumerable number of such films to pick from in the genre to stream right now. So let’s narrow them down for you.

These are the most harrowing and ghoulish horror movies actually *set* at Halloween…

## Halloween

![Editorial use only Mandatory Credit: Photo by ITV/REX/Shutterstock (794253e) 'Halloween' Film - 1978 - Michael Myers (Tony Moran) wearing the mask, looks over the top of the stairs holding a knife. GTV ARCHIVE](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/SEI_36961042-10b8-e1793197385120.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646)

We have no choice here, really. We have to start this list with the most obvious – and arguably best – example of what we’re talking about.

There’s not another Halloween-set horror movie out there that quite encapsulates the terror that’s supposed to be associated with October 31.

Contrary to popular belief, [John Carpenter’s](https://metro.co.uk/tag/john-carpenter/) seminal slasher [Halloween](https://metro.co.uk/2021/02/26/halloweens-john-carpenter-on-enduring-importance-of-horror-films-14150659/) isn’t the first of its kind, but it’s undeniably the most influential.

It launched [Jamie Lee Curtis](https://metro.co.uk/tag/jamie-lee-curtis/)’ career. It featured a fella in a William Shatner mask painted white, stabbing girls. It showcased *that* iconic theme tune. A true blood-soaked classic.

***Where to watch: BBC iPlayer, Shudder, Pluto TV, and Cultpix***

## House of 1000 Corpses

![](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/shutterstock_editorial_1576282a-5ec3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646)

Former frontman of heavy metallers White Zombie, Rob Zombie made [his directorial debut](https://metro.co.uk/2025/10/04/horror-masterpieces-inspired-ed-gein-new-netflix-series-streaming-now-24329986/) with this messy gorefest.

Alright, so it’s not likely to be studied in many film schools, but if you like your horror vile, violent, and totally moral-free, then this sadistic piece of grindhouse trash should be an annual watch.

Starring Sid Haig, Sheri Moon Zombie, and Bill Moseley, House of 1000 Corpses follows a group of friends who pick up a hitchhiker.

When their car breaks down, they travel to the hitchhiker’s family home, which just so happens to be close by, and find themselves imprisoned and tortured by the sadistic Firefly family.

***Where to watch: Shudder, Plex, and Lionsgate+***

# North East production company celebrates international film premiere

### A new film from Candle & Bell, exploring loneliness and the search for human connection, will make its world premiere at a major Greek film festival

![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!rn4b!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fbe1f105f-4f10-41dc-82b7-8e3b812619a1_1500x1135.jpeg)

Gateshead-based production company Candle & Bell is preparing for an international premiere after its latest film, *The Date*, was selected for the 67th Thessaloniki International Film Festival.

It will receive its world premiere on November 7 as part of *Taming Time*, a new festival strand showcasing unconventional approaches to the moving image.

Starring Jazmín Falak, the film follows Jazmín, a Spanish single mother living in London, as she prepares nervously for her first date in years.

What begins with anticipation gradually gives way to disappointment in a near-silent exploration of loneliness, heartbreak and the need for human connection.

The film was directed by London-based filmmaker Alex Barrett, who co-wrote the screenplay with Áine O’Neill-Mason, and produced by Candle & Bell’s Maria Caruana Galizia alongside Oscar-winning producer Julie Foy.

![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!p2Zm!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F5936a7bf-db89-47b8-a19a-424bb3858bdf_1500x1135.jpeg)

Maria said: “We shot *The Date* in just four days, in long, unbroken takes, because we wanted audiences to live through every minute with Jazmín, from the nervous excitement of the morning to the disappointment that follows.

“It’s a film about the particular loneliness of heartbreak in a city that doesn’t quite feel like home.

“Thessaloniki has a long history of championing bold, formally adventurous cinema, and we couldn’t ask for a better place to share it with the world for the first time.”

Director Alex Barrett added: “When I set out to make *The Date*, I did so with the intention of making a film that grips the viewer through human emotions; that is, through internal, rather than external, action.”

He praised the performance of Jazmín Falak, whose previous credits include Netflix’s *The Kingdom*, adding: “In Jazmín, I found a more-than-perfect partner. I can’t wait for everyone to witness her spellbinding performance.”

The film has been selected for *Taming Time*, a new festival strand dedicated to works which explore unconventional approaches to the moving image.

Producer Julie Foy said: “*The Date* is ultimately a film about our basic human need for connection, communication and acceptance in a world that can be extremely brutal and unforgiving.”

Candle & Bell has previously received support through the BBC Small Indie Fund on three occasions and has a growing slate of film and television projects in development with broadcasters including Film4 and the BBC.

Its credits include the BBC Radio 4 sitcom *Tom & Lauren Are Going OOT!*, while upcoming projects include *SCRUM*, written by Bethan Moore, and *Gunners*, by Lucy Brydon.

![an image, when javascript is unavailable](https://sb.scorecardresearch.com/p?c1=2&c2=6035310&c4=&cv=3.9&cj=1)

# ‘Ah Girl’ Wins Best Film at Singapore’s Silver Screen Awards as Shahrbanoo Sadat Takes Director Prize

By
[Naman Ramachandran](https://variety.com/author/saharanaman-ramachandran/)

### [Naman Ramachandran](https://variety.com/author/saharanaman-ramachandran/)

#### Latest

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/src/svg/icons/google-preferred.svg)
![Ah Girl](https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Ah-Girl.jpg?w=1000&h=667&crop=1)

Singaporean filmmaker Ang Geck Geck Priscilla’s debut feature “[Ah Girl](https://variety.com/t/ah-girl/)” won best film in the Asian Feature Film Competition at the [Singapore International Film Festival](https://variety.com/t/singapore-international-film-festival/)’s Silver Screen Awards on Saturday.

The film follows a seven-year-old girl in 1990s Singapore whose parents have separated. Ang workshopped the project at the festival’s Southeast Asian Film Lab back in 2015, and “Ah Girl” went on to take the Youth Jury Award at the International Film Festival Rotterdam. Ang is an alumna of the Busan Asian Film Academy. Her 2012 short “Broken Crayon” won the Singapore Short Film Awards’ best short film prize.

## Related Stories

[![View Conference](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)](https://variety.com/2026/film/global/god-of-war-mandalorian-grogu-cinema-gaming-view-1236909776/)

### [‘God of War’s’ Bruno Velazquez, ‘Mandalorian & Grogu’s’ Hal Hickel Detail Cinema-Gaming Crossover at View Conference](https://variety.com/2026/film/global/god-of-war-mandalorian-grogu-cinema-gaming-view-1236909776/)

## Related Stories

![View Conference](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

### [‘God of War’s’ Bruno Velazquez, ‘Mandalorian & Grogu’s’ Hal Hickel Detail Cinema-Gaming Crossover at View Conference](https://variety.com/2026/film/global/god-of-war-mandalorian-grogu-cinema-gaming-view-1236909776/)

Afghan filmmaker [Shahrbanoo Sadat](https://variety.com/t/shahrbanoo-sadat/) won best director for “No Good Men,” which opened the Berlinale. Set in Kabul just before the Taliban come back to power, the drama follows a camerawoman whose work, family and freedom are suddenly in doubt. Sadat, who has lived in Germany since 2021, made the 2016 Cannes premiere “Wolf and Sheep” and 2019’s “The Orphanage.”

The jury split the best performance prize. Pushpa Thing Lama was honored for “Elephants in the Fog,” about a member of Nepal’s third-gender Kinnar community searching for her missing daughter. Putri Marino shared the award for “Four Seasons in Java,” a magical realist drama about a woman who goes back to her hometown after two decades behind bars.

The Special Jury Prize went to Japanese director Nagahisa Makoto’s “Burn,” his second feature, which premiered at Sundance. Nagahisa won awards at the same festival for his short “And So We Put Goldfish in the Pool” (2017) and his feature “We Are Little Zombies” (2019).

In the Southeast Asian Short Film Competition, Yogyakarta-based artist-filmmaker Arief Budiman’s “Golden Island” was named best Southeast Asian short. The film, which competed at Rotterdam, follows a videographer from Java and another from Papua as they make a film about Papua together. Thai director Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke won best director for “The Bovine Comedy,” a Locarno premiere set in a 2036 where cows have nearly died out. His feature debut “A Useful Ghost” (2025) won the Critics’ Week Grand Prize at Cannes and received a special mention at SGIFF.

German-Indonesian filmmaker Berthold Wahjudi took the shorts Special Jury Prize for “‘Vaterland’ or A Bule Named Yanto,” which premiered in Cannes’ Critics’ Week. Sarah Lingam won best performance for “Flame of the Forest,” about a young nurse who returns home and is blamed for her grandmother’s death. Singaporean experimental animator Exyl’s “Singapore God” was named best Singapore short.

The Audience Choice Award went to Singapore Panorama Programme 2, “Second Life, Second Skin,” a package of five shorts: Shara Tay’s “Kiss Me Climax,” Ash Goh Hua’s “Subterranea,” Syahmi Iman’s “Reanimator,” Leon Cheo’s “Orang Minyak” and Ewan Leong’s “Encik.”

Prizes were also handed out at the SGIFF Pro Pitching Forum, held Oct. 30. “Agape,” from Yamaguchi Shin and Miyahara Takuya, won the SGIFF Pro Pitching Forum Award. The SGIFF Pro Pitching Forum Award (Asian Producers Network) went to Lệ Diễm Hà’s “Dear Son An.” Tong Khoon Mun and Zhou Ke Xin’s “Beg, Borrow, Steal” won the SGIFF Abroad Award supported by Sony, and Sam Chua Weishi and Rein Maychaelson’s “Primal” received the SGIFF Abroad Award.

Earlier in the festival, Indian star Aamir Khan received the SGIFF Screen Icon Award from Peter Chan during [an In Conversation With session](https://variety.com/2026/film/festivals/aamir-khan-tears-up-3-idiots-2-andaz-apna-apna-2-updates-1236920409/) on Oct. 22. Kore-eda Hirokazu, who released two features this year, “Sheep in the Box” and “Look Back,” was [presented with the SGIFF Cinema Honorary Award](https://variety.com/2026/film/festivals/kore-eda-hirokazu-why-never-films-children-crying-1236930180/) by Boo Junfeng on Oct. 24.

The ceremony took place at the Singtel Waterfront Theatre on the penultimate day of the 37th SGIFF, which runs through Nov. 1. Launched in 1991, the Silver Screen Awards was the first international film competition to include a dedicated section for Asian cinema.

The full list of winners:

**ASIAN FEATURE FILM COMPETITION**Best Film: “Ah Girl” – Ang Geck Geck  
Best Director: Shahrbanoo Sadat – “No Good Men”  
Best Performance: Pushpa Thing Lama – “Elephants in the Fog”; Putri Marino – “Four Seasons in Java”  
Special Jury Prize: “Burn” – Nagahisa Makoto

**SOUTHEAST ASIAN SHORT FILM COMPETITION**Best Southeast Asian Short Film: “Golden Island” – Arief Budiman  
Best Director: Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke – “The Bovine Comedy”  
Special Jury Prize: “‘Vaterland’ or A Bule Named Yanto” – Berthold Wahjudi  
Best Performance: Sarah Lingam – “Flame of the Forest”  
Best Singapore Short Film: “Singapore God” – Exyl

**AUDIENCE CHOICE AWARD**Singapore Panorama Program 2: “Second Life, Second Skin” – “Kiss Me Climax” (Shara Tay), “Subterranea” (Ash Goh Hua), “Reanimator” (Syahmi Iman), “Orang Minyak” (Leon Cheo), “Encik” (Ewan Leong)

**SGIFF PRO PITCHING FORUM AWARDS**SGIFF Pro Pitching Forum Award: “Agape” – Yamaguchi Shin, Miyahara Takuya  
SGIFF Pro Pitching Forum Award (Asian Producers Network): “Dear Son An” – Lệ Diễm Hà  
SGIFF Abroad Award supported by Sony: “Beg, Borrow, Steal” – Tong Khoon Mun, Zhou Ke Xin  
SGIFF Abroad Award: “Primal” – Sam Chua Weishi, Rein Maychaelson

**SPECIAL RECOGNITION AWARDS**SGIFF Screen Icon Award: Aamir Khan  
SGIFF Cinema Honorary Award: Kore-eda Hirokazu

# Istanbul Film Festival to bring together global and Turkish cinema in April

![Visitors gather at a venue hosting an Istanbul Film Festival event organized by the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts (IKSV) in Istanbul, Türkiye. (AA Photo)](https://img.turkiyetoday.com/images/2026/10/31/istanbul-film-festival-to-bring-together-global-and-turkish-cinema-in-april-3231376_20261031002010.jpg)

![Photo](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/i-foto.svg)

![BigPhoto](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/i-fotobuyut.svg)

Visitors gather at a venue hosting an Istanbul Film Festival event organized by the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts (IKSV) in Istanbul, Türkiye. (AA Photo)

By  **[Newsroom](/author/newsroom)**

October 31, 2026 09:55 AM GMT+03:00

[![Newsletters](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/s/i/add-preferred-source-g.png) Set as preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=turkiyetoday.com "Add as a preferred source on Google")  ![Share]()

![newsletters]()

The 46th Istanbul Film Festival will bring together international cinema, award-winning productions and Turkish films from April 8 to 18, 2027.

The 46th Istanbul Film Festival, organized by the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts (IKSV), will take place from April 8 to 18, 2027, bringing together new releases from world cinema, award-winning films from international festivals, Turkish productions and classic works.

According to a statement from IKSV, the festival will be held with sponsorship from N Kolay and will feature competitive screenings alongside special events and programs for film industry professionals.

## Three competitions to showcase filmmakers

The festival will feature three competitive sections: the Golden Tulip Competition, New Perspectives and the Short Film Competition.

While the Golden Tulip Competition will form part of the festival's competitive program, New Perspectives will focus on first or second feature-length films by Turkish filmmakers, providing a dedicated section for emerging talent.

The Short Film Competition will round out the festival's three competitive categories.

### Industry events and international cinema take center stage

Beyond its film screenings, the festival will offer discussions, special screenings and conversations that bring audiences together around cinema.

The program will also include Meetings on the Bridge, Türkiye's first co-production market, which provides training and networking opportunities for film industry professionals.

Applications for the festival open on Nov. 9. Details will be posted on IKSV’s official website.

# Kendal Mountain Festival announces 165-film programme

![Jade Jones Profile Image](/resources/images/21408859?type=thumb)

![USA Today logo](/resources/responsive-static/images/usa-today-logo.svg)

Kendal Mountain Festival has announced its International film programme, more than 165 films will be screened at a festival weekend dedicated to adventure storytelling and the outdoors.

Kendal Mountain Festival, taking place in Cumbria from November 19 to 22, will feature 26 world premieres, 48 UK premieres and 25 European premieres as part of its International Film Programme.

The films, selected from more than 650 submissions to the Kendal Mountain International Film Competition, celebrate adventure storytelling and the human spirit in the outdoors.

![]()Just Climber : Cap ou pas Cap ? *(Image: Kendal Mountain Festival)*

![]()

Jacqui Scott, CEO of Kendal Mountain Festival, said: "There’s a moment in a darkened cinema, just as a film lands, when the whole room goes still – nobody’s anywhere else.

"That’s what Presence means to us this year, and it’s what these filmmakers give us: the chance to be somewhere else entirely, yet completely here at the same time.

"We are so grateful that over 650 of them trusted us with their ways of seeing this year, from world premieres with the outdoor world’s leading athletes to first films from brave and exciting new voices.

"So come to Kendal, linger a while, and be here, fully here, with us and these wonderful films."

The competition will be judged by an independent panel of film and outdoor industry experts and will feature 12 prize categories, including Best Short, Best Adventure and Exploration, Best Environment, Best Climbing and the coveted Grand Prize.

An audience-voted People’s Choice award will also be presented.

The Kendal Mountain International Film Awards ceremony will take place in front of a live audience on Saturday, November 21, at 7.45pm.

A highlight of this year’s festival is the 2026 Festival Trailer, titled Presence, which features clips from 128 selected films and words by poet laureate and author Helen Mort.

The festival will also host a series of industry events aimed at established and emerging adventure filmmakers, including workshops, networking sessions and panel discussions.

New for 2026 is the KendalPitch initiative, launched in partnership with Beyond Boundaries Films, which will award a £10,000 grant to an emerging filmmaker.

Five shortlisted filmmakers will pitch their ideas to an international jury in front of a live audience on Saturday, November 21, at 6.15pm.

![]()We Are Here *(Image: Kendal Mountain Festival)*

![]()

For those unable to attend in person, the 2026 Kendal Mountain International Film Programme will be available on demand via the festival’s streaming platform, Kendal Mountain Player, starting Thursday, November 19.

The festival has also launched The Film Edit, a new initiative that will bring seven curated screenings to independent cinemas across the UK during the festival weekend.

Film guide and tickets [here.](https://tickets.kendalmountainfestival.com/Film_Guides?ref=ed_direct)

![Ipswich.co.uk](https://storage.ghost.io/c/29/1e/291e4b7f-e551-4458-b546-61963954b22f/content/images/2026/03/logotype-no-ext-1.svg)

# Ipswich International Film Festival opens with Halloween vampire classic

The first Ipswich International Film Festival (IIFF) opens at King Street Cinema on Saturday, 31 October, with a 35mm screening of cult classic Shadow of the Vampire, followed by a Q&A with the film's producer, Richard Johns.

![Nicola Sebastian](https://storage.ghost.io/c/29/1e/291e4b7f-e551-4458-b546-61963954b22f/content/images/size/w160/2026/03/IMG_0815-1.jpeg)

#### [Nicola Sebastian](/author/nicola-sebastian/)

![Ipswich International Film Festival opens with Halloween vampire classic](https://storage.ghost.io/c/29/1e/291e4b7f-e551-4458-b546-61963954b22f/content/images/size/w1200/2026/10/IMG_0442-1.jpeg)

**Why it matters:** The fortnight-long festival brings premieres, previews and restorations to King Street Cinema in Ipswich - one of the only remaining UK cinemas that can still screen 35mm film.

**The details:** Directed by E. Elias Merhige, Shadow of the Vampire reimagines the making of F.W. Murnau's Nosferatu as "a dark fable of artistic obsession", according to organisers, who describe it as "the perfect Halloween movie".

**What to look out for:** The festival runs until Saturday, 14 November. Highlights include:

There will also be conversations with filmmakers Sophie Fiennes and Howard Berry, media consultant Adam Gee, and Ghostbusters documentary makers Claire Bueno and Anthony Bueno.

The programme includes tributes to filmmakers Russ Meyer, John Waters, Barbara Hammer and René Laloux.

**What they're saying:** Dan Champion, the festival's founder and artistic director, said: "Our inaugural year celebrates the outsiders, the pioneers, the mavericks and the rebels – those filmmakers who have challenged convention, expanded the language of film and redefined the way we see the world."

Organisers said the festival represents "confidence in cinema as an art form, in audiences as curious participants, and in the belief that the most enthralling stories are often found at the edges rather than the centre."

Lee Walker, chief executive of festival sponsor Ipswich Central, said: "We look forward to the IIFF being a milestone event in the calendar going forward."

**What's next:** Businesses across the town will offer discounts and deals to ticket holders, with full details to be published on the All About Ipswich website.

**The bottom line:** Ipswich's first international film festival opens on Halloween with a vampire cult classic, kicking off a fortnight of premieres, previews and 35mm screenings at one of the few cinemas in the UK still able to show them.
